chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and left a slave girl, having emancipated a third of her. So the executor married her before anything from the inheritance was distributed. That she is evaluated, and she and her husband are made to work to pay off the remainder of her price after being evaluated. So whatever of emancipation or enslavement befalls the woman, it flows upon her child.

key_terms.تُسْتَسْعَى: she is made to work/pay off

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave girl who is partially freed and married by the executor before inheritance distribution?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the fiqh of 'partial manumission' (itq nisf) where the executor marries the slave-girl, establishing that her valuation and subsequent payment of the remaining price are treated as estate expenses. It highlights the Shia legal principle that the child's status is dynamically linked to the mother's final state of freedom or servitude after this settlement, reflecting the interplay between inheritance law and marital contracts in early Islamic jurisprudence.
